result:
**The proposed answer of 0 is wrong.** An explicit admissible function gives a nonzero value of the quantity, so the supremum is positive.

**Coefficient formulas.** For $f(z)=z+a_2z^2+a_3z^3+a_4z^4+\cdots$, the inverse coefficients are $A_2=-a_2$, $A_3=2a_2^2-a_3$, $A_4=-(5a_2^3-5a_2a_3+a_4)$. Expanding $\log(f^{-1}(w)/w)$ gives:

- $\Gamma_1=-\tfrac{a_2}{2}$
- $\Gamma_2=\tfrac{3}{4}a_2^2-\tfrac{a_3}{2}$
- $\Gamma_3=-\tfrac{5}{3}a_2^3+2a_2a_3-\tfrac{a_4}{2}$

Hence
$$\Gamma_1\Gamma_3-\Gamma_2^2=\tfrac{13}{48}a_2^4-\tfrac14a_2^2a_3+\tfrac14a_2a_4-\tfrac14a_3^2.$$

**Extremal candidate.** Take $1+\frac{zf''}{f'}=e^z$. Since $e^z$ is convex and univalent, $f$ is convex and hence univalent, so $f\in\mathcal{C}_e$. Equivalently, $f'(z)=\exp\!\big(\int_0^z \frac{e^t-1}{t}\,dt\big)$, which gives
$$f'(z)=1+z+\tfrac34z^2+\tfrac{17}{36}z^3+\cdots,$$
so $a_2=\tfrac12$, $a_3=\tfrac14$, $a_4=\tfrac{17}{144}$. (These also follow from matching $zf''/f'$ with $e^z$ term by term.)

**Evaluation.**
$$\frac{13}{48}\cdot\frac1{16}-\frac14\cdot\frac18\cdot\frac14\cdot 2\,(\text{i.e. }\tfrac14a_2^2a_3=\tfrac1{64})+\frac14\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac{17}{144}-\frac14\cdot\frac1{16}$$

Over the common denominator 2304 the four terms are $\tfrac{39}{2304}-\tfrac{36}{2304}+\tfrac{34}{2304}-\tfrac{36}{2304}$, so the value is
$$\Gamma_1\Gamma_3-\Gamma_2^2=\frac{1}{2304}\neq 0.$$

Therefore the supremum of $|\Gamma_1\Gamma_3-\Gamma_2^2|$ is at least $1/2304>0$. The proposed reasoning is also unsupported: it cites no specific theorem and then asserts the discriminant vanishes, which the example above contradicts. I have not determined the exact supremum.

VERDICT: REJECT
